question: What is the primary contrast agent used in a barium swallow procedure?
explanation: Barium sulfate is a dense radiopaque medium that coats the mucosal lining to make the upper gastrointestinal tract visible on X-rays. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why is barium used instead of standard X-rays alone for esophageal evaluation?

options.A: It numbs the throat during the test
options.C: It permanently stains abnormal tissue areas
options.D: It outlines soft tissue contours clearly

explanation: Soft tissues do not show up well on normal X-rays, so barium provides the necessary contrast to highlight the lining. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which condition is an absolute contraindication for using barium sulfate contrast?
explanation: Barium escaping through a perforation into body cavities causes severe irritation and complications, requiring water-soluble contrast instead. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h2)

question: What happens if barium enters the lungs of a patient with high aspiration risk?
explanation: Aspiration of barium triggers an intense inflammatory response in the lung tissue, leading to serious respiratory complications. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h2)

question: How long should a patient typically fast before undergoing a barium swallow?
explanation: An empty stomach prevents residual food particles from obscuring small lesions and reduces the risk of aspiration. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h3)

question: Why is confirming pregnancy status important prior to a barium swallow examination?

options.A: To ensure the mother can swallow properly
options.C: To prevent fetal exposure to ionizing radiation
options.D: To stop the barium from mixing with amniotic fluid

explanation: Fluoroscopy uses X-rays, which pose potential developmental risks to a growing fetus during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is the purpose of using effervescent granules alongside barium during the test?

options.B: Preventing nausea from the contrast taste
options.C: Numbing the back of the throat
options.D: Creating a double-contrast view of the mucosa

explanation: Gas produced by the granules coats the barium-lined walls, providing a sharp double-contrast image of the mucosal surface. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why does the radiologist ask the patient to change positions frequently during fluoroscopy?

options.A: To push the barium faster into the large intestine
options.B: To help the patient stay awake during the procedure
options.C: To view the esophagus and stomach from different angles
options.D: To prevent dizziness from standing too long

explanation: Oblique and angled views ensure hidden lesions or abnormalities are not missed behind overlapping anatomical structures. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h4)

question: What characteristic shape does the lower esophagus show in patients with achalasia?
explanation: Achalasia prevents the lower esophageal sphincter from relaxing, creating a tapered bird-beak look on the barium study. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h5)

question: How do esophageal varices typically present on a barium swallow image?
explanation: Dilated submucosal veins bulge into the lumen, creating irregular, serpentine or worm-like impressions against the barium. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h5)

question: What common side effect should nurses warn patients to expect after a barium swallow?

options.A: Bright red blood in the urine
options.B: Complete loss of appetite for a week
options.C: Chalky white or light gray stools

explanation: The elimination of residual barium sulfate naturally turns the patient's stool a pale, chalky color for a few days. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h6)

question: A patient asks for advice two hours after completing a barium swallow. What instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Take strong antacids to clear residual contrast
options.B: Remain on strict bed rest for the rest of the day
options.C: Increase fluid intake and take prescribed laxatives
options.D: Avoid eating until stools return to normal color

explanation: Fluids and laxatives prevent the barium from hardening in the colon and causing severe constipation or impaction. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h6)
